cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, has just counted every man twenty and older who can serve in the army. That's a LOT of people, friend. Now the LORD speaks to Moses and his brother Aaron, and the big question is: where do you PUT everybody?

cards.question: The LORD tells the Israelites to camp all the way around something. What sits at the center of it all?
True or false: the LORD tells the tribes to pitch their tents right up against the Tent of Meeting.

cards.text: They camp at a distance, each man under his standard, with the banners of his family. In my junk drawer we didn't have banners. We had a takeout menu and a rubber band, and we were GRATEFUL.

cards.question: The LORD starts with the east side of the camp, toward the sunrise. Which tribe's divisions camp there?

cards.text: Judah's leader is Nahshon son of Amminadab, with 74,600 men in his division. The tribes of Issachar and Zebulun camp right next to them.

cards.question: The camp of Judah has 186,400 men in all. When Israel moves, the LORD says they shall set out ___.

cards.text: On the south side, it's the camp of Reuben, led by Elizur son of Shedeur, with Simeon and Gad beside them. That's 151,450 men, and they set out second.
Okay, east and south are set. But before the LORD gets to the other two sides, He talks about the middle. The part everybody's camped around.

cards.question: When Israel is on the move, who travels with the Tent of Meeting in the middle of the camps?
True or false: when they set out, each tribe travels in the same order it camped, in its own place under its standard.

cards.text: West side: the camp of Ephraim, led by Elishama son of Ammihud, with Manasseh and Benjamin beside them. That's 108,100 men, and they set out third.
That leaves one side. The north. Somebody's getting it, and I'm sitting here like it's the last cookie on the tray.

cards.question: East, south and west are taken. Which tribe's divisions camp on the north side?

cards.text: Dan's leader is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai. Asher and Naphtali camp beside them, and the whole camp of Dan comes to 157,600 men.

cards.question: True or false: the camp of Dan sets out right behind the camp of Judah.

cards.text: Add up all four camps and you get 603,550 men. SIX. HUNDRED. THOUSAND. Friend, I used to get nervous when six cookie cutters shared one counter.

cards.question: Not everybody is in that count of 603,550. Which tribe isn't counted among the other Israelites?
So how do the Israelites handle the LORD's plan for camping and setting out?

answers.text: They follow only part of it
They swap a few of the spots

findings.problem: Card 1 states two facts from outside the passage with no reference: the census of every man twenty and older who can serve in the army (Numbers 1:2-3, 45-46) and Aaron being Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14). The card cites only Numbers 2:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Earlier story cards rule out both wrong answers. Card 8 places Simeon on the south side, and card 10 puts the Levites in the middle with the Tent of Meeting. That leaves Dan as the only possible pick for the north side.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 8 already says Reuben's camp sets out second, and card 12 says Ephraim's sets out third. So the baker already knows Dan can't set out right behind Judah, and the answer is given away before the question is asked.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers are already ruled out. Card 6 counts Judah in the camps and card 12 counts Benjamin. Card 17 adds up 'all four camps', and card 10 put the Levites in the middle, outside the four camps. Levi is the only answer left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Cards 6, 8, 12 and 15 read as flat lists of leaders, tribes and totals with none of Papa Dorin's voice. Only cards 4, 13 and 17 carry any personality, so most of the walkthrough reads like a roster instead of a storyteller.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Numbers 2:3-31 is almost entirely leaders' names and census numbers for each tribe, which fits the long-stretch list ('genealogies and name lists', 'census counts and numbers'). If it counts as a long stretch, it should get one summary story card and no choice cards. Instead it gets four summary cards (6, 8, 12, 15) and four choice cards (5, 7, 14, 16). But the camp layout and the marching order are also the heart of this passage, and treating the whole stretch as one card would leave almost nothing to ask.
findings.question: When a long stretch makes up nearly the whole passage, does the long-stretch rule still apply? Should the camp positions and marching order in Numbers 2:3-31 get choice cards while only the leaders and numbers are summed up, or should the whole stretch be one story card with no choice cards?
